title: Pentagon Launches Task Force Iron Gate to Cut Off Iran's Land and Caspian Supply Lines
snippet: Expanding beyond its months-long naval blockade, the U.S. military is standing up a new Tampa-based task force to crack down on Iranian land commerce, weapons smuggling, and illicit revenue streams.
content:
WASHINGTON — The Pentagon is expanding its pressure campaign against Tehran beyond the high seas, establishing a specialized military task force dedicated to severing Iran’s overland smuggling corridors and Caspian Sea trade routes, U.S. officials announced Saturday.

Building on a months-long naval blockade in the Middle East, Task Force Iron Gate will focus on curbing Tehran’s transport of advanced weaponry, dual-use technology, and sanctioned goods. Headquartered out of U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) in Tampa, Florida, the unit will coordinate closely with key federal partners, including the Treasury, State, and Justice departments, as well as the U.S. intelligence community.

Targeting Covert Supply Routes

“Strengthening CENTCOM’s collaboration with U.S. interagency partners will further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military,” Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of Central Command, said in a statement.

The creation of the task force comes after investigative reports exposed Iran's reliance on a shadow network of military agencies to evade existing sanctions and maritime blockades. Since early 2025, Iran has managed to import over $2 billion in military hardware, explosives, and heavy-duty vehicles using cargo ships across the Caspian Sea from Russia, overland trucking routes through Central Asia, and air freight shipments from China.

While CENTCOM estimates that its naval operations in the Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Sea have effectively frozen more than $25 billion in Iranian crude oil sales, Tehran’s land-based channels have allowed the regime to maintain a steady flow of crucial supplies.

Political Friction and Escalation Risks

The push to close Iran’s trade loopholes arrives during a period of heightened geopolitical and domestic political tension. Following recent U.S. midterm elections that saw significant gains for opposition Democrats, some political figures—including Vice President JD Vance—have publicly questioned the overall cost and direction of the conflict.

Despite U.S. and Israeli military strikes inflicting severe damage on Iran’s conventional armed forces, Tehran’s leadership maintains a firm grip on domestic power. Furthermore, U.S. intelligence assessments indicate that additional strikes are unlikely to force major diplomatic concessions from Iranian leadership.

As international mediators work frantically to negotiate a cease-fire, regional partners across the Gulf remain on high alert amid concerns that any renewed offensive could trigger widespread retaliatory attacks against critical energy infrastructure.
